subject: Billing breach: spend-cap guardrails & emergency mitigation
body:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: What happens when we blow past our monthly budget?

Hi Soojin,

Quick question from our billing team — we ran into a usage spike last night during a batch of model evaluations and want to understand the exact behavior if we exceed the budget we've set in the console. Specifically:

- Will Redwood automatically stop serving requests (hard cap)?
- Will requests continue and we get billed at overage rates?
- Is there an emergency throttle or soft cap we can enable to avoid surprises?

We need this detail to finalize our procurement paperwork. We may be asking for a short-term spike allowance but want a clear fallback if the spike grows.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Gomez
Director, AI Engineering
BrightBridge Health

----
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@brightbridgehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 13:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: What happens when we blow past our monthly budget?

Hi Alex — thanks for the note and sorry about the late-night spike. Short answer up front: you can choose what happens. We support three primary guardrail behaviors for hosted API billing caps:

1) Soft cap (recommended default) — service continues, we send tiered alerts at 70%/85%/95% of your threshold. Overage is billed at the committed rate for the month plus an overage multiplier (configurable in contract).

2) Hard cap (billing cutoff) — traffic is blocked at the spend threshold. Calls receive 429/402 (configurable) and you can opt-in to an automatic fallback model (smaller cheaper model) for read-only workloads.

3) Emergency throttle (rate-limited fallback) — requests are accepted but rate-limited aggressively to keep latency within SLO and avoid unbounded spend; this is good for degraded but functional behavior during tests.

Operational notes:
- We can enable pre-authorized overage (one-time approvals) for specific spike windows to avoid manual PO delays.
- For enterprise deals, customers commonly pair a hard cap for day-to-day with a one-click emergency override that notifies your procurement and our CS manager.
- Overages are billed monthly and appear on the next invoice; we do not auto-charge corporate cards for ad-hoc spikes without prior agreement.

Attached is a short matrix that outlines recommended defaults, alert cadence, and the legal language we include for overage billing. I attached the short "Redwood-SpendCap-Options-v1.pdf" and a template emergency approval spreadsheet.

If you want, Ben (cc'd) can run through a quick demo in the console where we set a hard cap and simulate a throttle. Evelyn can walk through the emergency approval flow if you want procurement to see it.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Redwood-SpendCap-Options-v1.pdf (pdf)
- BBH-emergency-approval-form.xlsx (xlsx)

----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@brightbridgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 10:08:03 -0700
Subject: Re: What happens when we blow past our monthly budget? (console demo + proposal)

Alex / Soojin — quick follow-up from my side. For BrightBridge's usage profile (batch evals + interactive prod inference) I recommend the following starter configuration:

- Monthly committed baseline: 250M tokens (committed rate)
- Soft cap alerts at 70/85/95% that hit both your engineering and procurement aliases
- Hard cap enabled by default on production-keys, with an emergency override window of +20% available only via signed approval (DocuSign)
- Emergency throttle set to 10 RPS for production keys when hard cap is tripped (keeps the UI functional for admins)

I'll prepare a short AMP (Mutual Action Plan) and include a clause for a one-time spike allowance that requires a signed emergency approval form (attached). That way procurement doesn't see unexpected charges but your team can run controlled experiments.

I'll attach a proposed amendment to the SOW if you'd like to bake this in.

Cheers,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:15:20 -0700
Subject: Internal: quick approval needed for one-time spike credit?

Team — procurement at BBH is asking whether we can provide a one-time goodwill credit for the overnight spike while they finalize their purchase order. Their legal wants explicit line-item language:

- Credit amount: $8,500 (one-time, applied to next invoice)
- Condition: they sign the emergency approval form and enable hard cap post-credit period
- Expiry: must sign within 7 business days

Evelyn — can you confirm this is within our standard concession band? If not, I'll escalate to my manager.

Priyom
Principal Sales Lead

----
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 13:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: quick approval needed for one-time spike credit?

Priyom / Ben — approved. $8,500 is within the standard concession range for a deal this size (deal > $250k ARR / strategic healthcare vertical). Condition the credit on:
1) BBH enabling hard cap on all production keys by EOD on the day the credit is issued, and
2) Signing the emergency approval DocuSign for +20% spike allowance.

I'll notify finance to expect the invoice adjustment. Soojin — please confirm with Alex and get the DocuSign completed.

Evelyn
Senior Customer Success Manager

----
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightbridgehealth.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: What happens when we blow past our monthly budget?

Thanks for the quick turnaround, everyone. Procurement is happy with the proposed controls. We accept the $8,500 one-time credit under the two conditions below and will sign the DocuSign this morning:

- We will enable the hard cap on the production keys after the credit is applied.
- We will complete the emergency approval DocuSign to allow a single +20% window (authorized by our VP Engineering) for up to 72 hours.

Please send the DocuSign link and the amended SOW language and we'll route through legal. Also — can Ben run the console demo next Tuesday at 10am PT to show how the hard cap and throttle behave?

Appreciate it,
Alex
